title: Up 50%, down 50%: back to even?
hook: A gain and a loss of the same size. Do they cancel out?

knows: how to take a percentage of a number
doesNotKnow: that a gain and an equal-size percentage loss do not cancel, because they apply to different bases
how big a percentage gain or loss is needed to undo another

misconception: Up 50% then down 50% gets me back to even.
objective: The learner can explain that percentage changes multiply on the current value, so +50% then −50% leaves 75%, undoing +50% needs −33⅓%, and undoing −50% needs +100%.

claims.text: Undoing a 50% rise needs a fall of 33⅓%: $150 × ⅔ = $100.
Undoing a 50% fall needs a rise of 100%.
The order of percentage changes does not matter: −50% then +50% also gives $75.
Recovering from any loss needs a larger percentage gain than the loss.
claims.source: After a loss of x (0 < x < 1), the needed gain is 1/(1 − x) − 1 = x/(1 − x) > x.

claims.text: The numbers are a made-up example, not a claim about any market.

recall.question: A price falls 20%. What rise brings it back to where it started?
recall.why: The rise is taken from the smaller value: 0.8 × 1.25 = 1. Percent changes multiply, so recovery needs a bigger percentage than the loss.
